problem:
Consider the set $B,$ defined as

$$
B={\frac{1}{2}(4)^{n}:n\in Z,\,-1\le n\le 2}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $B?$
worked_solution:
The condition after the "$:$" symbol

$$
n\in Z,\,-1\le n\le 2
$$

states that $n$ can be any integer number that satisfies the inequality $-1\le n\le 2.$ In other words, 

$$
n={-1,0,1,2}.
$$

Therefore, the elements of $B$ are all the terms of the sequence ${b}_{n},$ given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{1}{2}(4)^{n},\,n\in {-1,0,1,2}.
$$

Let's write down all the terms of our sequence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{-1} & =\frac{1}{2}(4)^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{8} \\ {b}_{0} & =\frac{1}{2}(4)^{0}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1=\frac{1}{2} \\ {b}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(4)^{1}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4=2 \\ {b}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(4)^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 16=8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
B={\frac{1}{8},\frac{1}{2},2,8}.
$$
